subject: Pricing & migration: dedicated commit proposal + conversion credits (Orbis Health)
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@orbishealth.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbishealth.ai, Victor Chen <victor.chen@orbishealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing & migration credits question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — Orbis was impressed with the latency numbers and the KV cache examples. We're starting to build the business case to migrate a subset of our traffic from your Hosted API to a Dedicated GPU pool. Before we loop procurement I wanted to understand three items so we can size the internal ask:  

1) How do you calculate conversion credits when moving committed hosted spend to a Reserved Dedicated commit? Is it a straight USD-for-USD offset, or do you apply a multiplier depending on predictable throughput?

2) Can Redwood provide a "bridge month" arrangement for the first 2 months after we cutover, where overage tolerance is increased while we optimize batching and prefixes?

3) For a target 10 rps sustained at p95 response time <= 200ms for our 16k-context models (mix of 8K/16K), what GPU pool sizing do you recommend and what throughput SLA would that carry?

If you can send a short proposal/ballpark numbers we can take that to procurement and our CFO. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Infrastructure, Orbis Health

Attachments: none

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@orbishealth.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing & migration credits question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the thoughtful note and glad the demo was useful. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with a short PDF proposal that includes a sample commit structure and bridge-month mechanics.

1) Conversion credits: We do a USD-for-USD conversion but apply a workload multiplier when the historical hosted spend is bursty or heavily over-indexed on embeddings vs. generations. Practically, for stable generation workloads like yours we usually apply a 0.9 multiplier (i.e., $1 hosted => $0.90 in committed credit) to reflect operational uplift and reserved pricing profile. We can adjust this (0.85–0.95) based on visibility into request shape.

2) Bridge months: Yes — we offer a 2-month bridge by default for migrations that meet the minimum commit threshold. During bridge months: 1) increased overage tolerance (20% over commit before overage pricing), 2) temporary burst pool for 2x baseline throughput for 30 minutes/day, and 3) joint optimization hours (1 day of engineering support) to tune batching and prefix caching.

3) Sizing: For your stated 10 RPS p95 <= 200ms on 16k-context models, likely a 4x A100-80GB or 8x L40s pool (depending on quantization) with continuous batching and KV cache. That maps to a baseline commit of ~1.2M tokens/day (~$45k/month in dedicated commit) with a 99.5% throughput SLO and 95% latency SLO at our defined traffic envelope. I'll outline options (conservative / recommended / aggressive) in the PDF.

I'll attach the draft proposal and put Rachel on copy for legal/terms input. Would love to set a 30-min walkthrough Wed or Thu.

—Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orbis_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.pdf

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@orbishealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing & migration credits question

Thanks Jordan and Samantha — quick legal/contracting notes from my side:  

- Conversion credits are applied at signature as a one-time contra to the first 12 months of committed invoices and amortized monthly on the invoice. We can front-load more credit into month 1 if needed for budgetary reasons.
- Bridge month terms must be appended to the SOW and include a clear cutover acceptance criteria (we suggest a 2-week stabilization window with agreed telemetry).
- For the proposed burst pool, we typically gate use by a signed escalation policy to avoid misuse.

Samantha — if procurement needs a sample SOW clause I can drop a redline.

Rachael Kim
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

Cc: Victor Chen <victor.chen@orbishealth.ai>, procurement@orbishealth.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing & migration credits question

Jordan/Rachel — thanks, this is super helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement's side:  

- Procurement asks whether the 0.9 multiplier is negotiable with a larger multi-year commit; they prefer USD-for-USD if we move 24 months upfront.
- They also asked if the 20% overage tolerance during bridge months can be extended to 30% provided there is a usage guardrail and a pre-agreed remediation playbook.

We're aiming to share a recommended commitment to our CFO by Friday. Do you have a version with tiered conversion credit options and an explicit example invoice showing the amortization?

Best,
Samantha

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing & migration credits question

Looping in a quick pricing steering note — Jordan, for enterprise deals with potential multi-year lock we can make the conversion credit effectively 1:1 at >18 month committed terms but we should keep a clause that allows a 10% reconciliation if the customer re-architects to a significantly lower cost profile (e.g., 2x more quantization). For the bridge overage tolerance, +10% (to 30%) is fine if procurement signs the escalation policy and we schedule the joint tuning week within the first 30 days.

If Jordan wants to present an options table to Orbis, I recommend:  
- Option A (12mo): 0.9 conversion multiplier, standard bridge (20% overage)
- Option B (24mo): 1.0 conversion multiplier, bridge extended to 30%, 5% prepaid discount on commit
- Option C (36mo): 1.0 conversion multiplier, bridge 30%, 7.5% prepaid discount, dedicated onboarding support (2 weeks)

Ben Carter
VP, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks, we've put together three options attached (conservative/recommended/aggressive) and an example amortized invoice for Option B (24mo). Key points:  

- Option B shows a 1:1 conversion at signature for 24-month prepays with a 30% bridge overage tolerance, amortized credit across months 1–24. Example invoice demonstrates month 1 gross commit, applied conversion credit, and net due.
- We've included the SOW redline language for bridge months, acceptance criteria, and escalation policy.
- GPU sizing: recommended cluster (for your stated mix) is 6x L40s with quantization to int8 for lower cost; if you prefer A100s for model fidelity we listed the delta.

Next step: if procurement is comfortable, I'll send a draft term sheet + prefill DocuSign for the 24mo Option B and we can target an April 30 signature to hit your FY planning window. Happy to review the example invoice with your CFO — can you share a 30-min slot tomorrow?
